current_qualitative.3m: Kuehne+Nagel is the global #1 ocean freight forwarder and a top-3 air forwarder with scale economies shared and proprietary digital routing platforms (Seaexplorer). However, enterprise shippers face low switching costs and routinely tender shipping lanes across competing forwarders, leaving K+N as a price-taking intermediary without independent pricing power >= inflation across the freight cycle.
current_qualitative.note: Rejected at Gate 3b (Pricing & Proof of Moat). Kuehne+Nagel is an asset-light global forwarding leader with high return on equity and stable anchor ownership by Klaus-Michael Kühne. However, third-party logistics forwarding is structurally intermediated and subject to frequent customer RFQs; EBIT halved from 2022 peaks as global ocean/air freight spreads normalized, confirming that margins are market-driven rather than protected by proprietary pricing power.
current_qualitative.evidence: Group revenue declined from CHF 39.4B (2022) to CHF 23.8B (2023) and EBIT fell ~50% from CHF 3.76B to CHF 1.90B as abnormal pandemic supply-chain surcharges vanished. Core Sea and Air logistics volumes are re-tendered regularly by corporate customers on commodity freight rates with negligible customer lock-in.

current_qualitative.3m: Groupe ADP operates an unreplicable infrastructure monopoly across the Greater Paris air basin (Paris-CDG, Paris-Orly, and Le Bourget). Physical runway slot scarcity and environmental restrictions prevent competing hub development. Under its dual-till regulatory model, non-aeronautical retail (Extime Paris luxury duty-free JV with Lagardère) exercises exceptional unregulated pricing power over high-spending intercontinental travelers, while aeronautical charges adjust via economic regulation agreements.
current_qualitative.note: Rejected at Gate 5 (Management & Capital Allocation, Score = 0). Paris CDG and Orly are irreplaceable national infrastructure assets, but Groupe ADP is 50.6% owned by the French State and suffers from acute capital allocation and governance pathologies: recurring regulatory conflict with ART over allowed aeronautical charges, bureaucratic inertia, and value-destructive international M&A (GMR Airports in India, TAV in Turkey) that loaded the balance sheet with €8.57B in net debt (>13x net income) and caused large impairment charges (€330M in 2024).
current_qualitative.evidence: State-dominated corporate governance has directed massive capital into speculative overseas airport stakes (GMR in India, TAV in Turkey) instead of disciplined per-share compounding. Net financial debt reached €8.57B at year-end 2024 against normalized net income of €638M (and reported net income of €342M, hit by a €330M merger charge on Indian assets), depressing consolidated ROIC to ~5-7%.

current_qualitative.3m: Aena holds an unreplicable national spatial monopoly over 46 Spanish airports handling >99% of Spanish commercial air passenger traffic. High entry barriers (land acquisition, airspace constraints, environmental permitting) make competitive entry impossible. Pricing power is anchored by DORA regulatory inflation indexation on aeronautical tariffs and multi-year retail concession contracts with CPI-indexed Minimum Annual Guarantees (MAG). 5-year median ROIC of 16.5% proves moat durability. Main erosion risks stem from 5-year DORA regulatory resets and airline lobbying against tariff increases.
current_qualitative.note: Passes all 6 gates (Quality pass). Unreplicable statutory monopoly operating the entire Spanish commercial airport network, benefiting from Spain's structural status as the world's #2 tourist destination. Aeronautical tariffs protected by DORA inflation indexation, while commercial retail concessions (duty-free, F&B) deliver high-margin non-aero profit with minimum annual guarantees. 16.5% median ROIC, 98% FCF conversion, and strong balance sheet (Net Debt/NI 2.1x, interest coverage 12.3x). [5-10Y g: passenger volume 2.8% + tariff/commercial price 1.8% + commercial mix 0.8% - capex/D&A drag 0.4% + buybacks 0.0%]
current_qualitative.evidence: Multi-year GAAP ROIC expanded from 8.1% (2022) to 15.1% (2023), 17.9% (2024), and 18.3% (2025), averaging 16.5% median. 2025 Owner EPS of €1.4245 surpassed pre-pandemic peaks. FCF conversion stands at 97.7%. Net debt of €4.41B is 2.06x 2025 net income (€2.14B) with 12.3x EBIT interest coverage.

current_qualitative.3m: Flughafen Zürich holds an irreplaceable infrastructure monopoly as Switzerland's primary gateway hub, operating under a federal concession valid through 2051. Severe geographical constraints in the Zurich basin and stringent environmental regulations make physical replication impossible. The model blends formulaic aeronautical tariffs with high-margin non-aero commercial retail and real estate (The Circle complex).
current_qualitative.note: Rejected at Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). While Zurich Airport is an irreplaceable physical infrastructure asset, aeronautical charges are governed by Swiss federal cost-plus return caps that hold multi-year ROIC to utility levels (~8.6%), while long-term runway growth is constrained by strict Swiss noise ordinances, a 23:00-06:00 curfew, contentious airspace negotiations with southern Germany, and high capex demands from the overseas Noida greenfield development in India.
current_qualitative.evidence: GAAP ROIC averages ~8.6% (6.05% in 2022, 8.61% in 2023, 9.05% in 2024, 8.60% in 2025), reflecting regulated utility-style asset return caps. Physical volume growth is tightly restricted by suburban noise politics and German airspace overflight restrictions, while heavy capex (CHF 550M-565M/yr) for domestic refurbishment and the Noida airport in India depresses free cash generation.

current_qualitative.3m: Entrenched architectural specification lock-in via certified hardware consultants embedding Schlage, Von Duprin, and LCN into Division 8/28 building schedules. Extreme switching costs from institutional master-key systems and strict life-safety fire/ADA compliance codes where liability prevents substitution. Empirical proof: 10-year median GAAP ROIC of 23.9% (operating tangible ROIC ~97%), stable ~42-44% gross margins, and consistent pricing realization exceeding inflation. Primary erosion threat is electronic access control disintermediation, though Allegion effectively embeds EAC into its mechanical door footprints.
current_qualitative.note: Passes all 6 gates. Global leader in commercial, institutional, and residential security hardware and access solutions. Wide moat anchored by architectural specification dominance (Schlage, Von Duprin, LCN) and high-switching-cost master key installed bases. Insulated from AI disruption with tailwinds from electronic access integration. Strong cash conversion (~92% FCF/NI) and conservative balance sheet (~1.5x net debt/EBITDA, 8.5x interest coverage). [5-10Y g: institutional volume 2.0% + pricing power 2.5% + electronic access mix & bolt-ons 2.5% - integration/R&D drag 0.5% + net buybacks 1.5%]
current_qualitative.evidence: 10-year median GAAP ROIC of 23.9% and tangible operating ROIC of 96.7%. 10-year FCF conversion averages ~98% of net income with capex under 2.5% of sales. Americas segment generates ~80%+ of revenue and >27% operating margins driven by non-residential institutional retrofit and replacement cycles. Pristine balance sheet with net debt to EBITDA of ~1.5x and EBIT/Interest coverage of 8.5x.

current_qualitative.3m: North American water heating duopoly (~35-37% residential share, >50% commercial share) protected by contractor-specified wholesale distribution (800+ independent supply houses) and professional plumber brand loyalty for same-day emergency replacements. Empirical proof includes a 10-year average GAAP ROIC above 20% (5Y median 21.2%, FY24-25 ~25-27%) and gross margin defense around 38-40% despite volatile steel and freight inflation. Key erosion threats include long-term disintermediation via retail big-box channels (Lowe's), Chinese domestic market price competition, and technological substitution during the transition to heat pumps.
current_qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 10, REJECT). Dominant North American water heater duopoly (~35-37% residential, >50% commercial share; 21.2% 5Y median ROIC) faces terminal runway constraints capped at 10 years due to active 5-macrotrend headwinds: [3] Geopolitical & China real estate secular contraction (~20% sales headwind from China property slump and aggressive domestic brand competition), and [4] Energy Transition disruption from DOE 2029 efficiency mandates requiring heat pump water heaters, which threatens legacy atmospheric tank economics and invites scaled HVAC conglomerate competition.
current_qualitative.evidence: Empirical financial track record shows strong historical capital efficiency: 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 21.2% (FY24 ~25%, FY25 ~26%), operating margins of 17-19%, and robust free cash flow conversion (>90-100% of net income; FY24 FCF $474M, FY25 FCF $546M). Balance sheet is pristine with total debt of ~$193M offset by cash and marketable securities (~$193M-$276M) and negligible net debt. Revenue breakdown: North America (~75-80% of sales, ~85% of EBIT) and Rest of World (~20-25% of sales, primarily China). While the North American wholesale plumbing channel creates an entrenched emergency replacement moat for legacy tanks, organic volume has stagnated (net sales flat at $3.85B in 2023, $3.82B in 2024, and $3.83B in 2025). The business faces secular growth caps and terminal disruption from the multi-year collapse of China's property market and the impending 2029 DOE regulatory shift toward heat pump water heating.

current_qualitative.3m: Carrier possesses brand recognition, a vast installed base, and entrenched dealer/distributor relationships in residential and commercial HVAC. However, it fails Gate 3b proof of moat: 5-year median GAAP ROIC has languished in the 6-8% range (2021: ~11%, 2022: ~8%, 2023: ~8%, 2024: ~6%, 2025: ~6-7%), well below the 12% hurdle. Carrier lacks the direct sales/service lock-in of Trane Technologies, relying heavily on two-step wholesale distribution where independent contractors face low barriers to switching between Carrier, Lennox, Trane, and Daikin. The €12B acquisition of Viessmann Climate Solutions at the peak of European heat pump subsidies in 2024 permanently diluted capital efficiency with >$10B of goodwill and intangibles, followed by severe residential volume contractions in Europe and North America.
current_qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12% & Inadequate Pricing Power, REJECT). While Carrier has a leading global footprint in HVAC equipment, its multi-cycle capital efficiency fails the Munger quality hurdle with a 5-year median GAAP ROIC of ~7% (peaking around 11% in 2021 and dipping to 5.6-7.1% in 2024-2025). The business relies on two-step wholesale distribution in residential HVAC, exposing it to distributor destocking, cyclical construction downturns, and direct competition from Daikin, Trane, and Lennox. Capital allocation was severely set back by the €12B peak-multiple acquisition of Viessmann in 2024, burdening the balance sheet and diluting returns right before a sharp European heat pump downturn.
current_qualitative.evidence: Multi-cycle financial track record shows GAAP ROIC consistently below hurdle: 2021 ~10.8-11.2%, 2022 ~8.3%, 2023 ~7.9%, 2024 ~5.6-6.8%, and 2025 ~5.8-7.1%, yielding a 5-year median of ~7.5% vs. the 12% requirement. GAAP operating margins have hovered around 8-11% (2021: 11.6%, 2023: 10.6%, 2024: 10.1%, 2025: ~8.3-10.0%), trailing direct peer Trane Technologies (17-19% operating margins, 20-25% ROIC). Carrier underwent a massive portfolio overhaul, divesting Fire & Security and Commercial Refrigeration to fund the €12B ($14.2B) acquisition of Viessmann Climate Solutions in early 2024. Despite applying ~$6B of divestiture proceeds to debt reduction, gross debt remains ~$12.3B with post-deal leverage near 2.8x-3.0x EBITDA. Viessmann suffered from post-acquisition residential volume contractions (-30% to -40% in European heat pumps in 2024-2025 following German subsidy revisions and gas price normalizations). Carrier lacks the direct sales branch model and high-margin recurring service attach rates of Trane, relying instead on two-step distribution through independent distributors (e.g., Watsco) and dealers.

current_qualitative.3m: High switching costs in proprietary building management systems (Metasys) and installed-base services, alongside York industrial chillers for mission-critical data center cooling; supported by tangible operating ROIC > 20% and demonstrated pricing power.
current_qualitative.note: Fails Gate 6 (Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet). Leading commercial HVAC and building automation provider fails Munger peace-of-mind balance sheet standards due to elevated leverage (long-term debt of $8.6B vs. FY25 net income of $1.7B, yielding LT debt / NI of ~5.1x vs. <=4.0x hurdle), persistent multi-year restructuring and separation expenses, negative tangible equity, and capital allocation prioritizing a $5.0B accelerated share repurchase over debt reduction. [5-10Y g: data center/commercial HVAC 4% + building services 3% + price 1% - restructuring drag -1%]
current_qualitative.evidence: Following the August 2025 close of the $8.1B sale ($5.0B net cash proceeds) of its Residential & Light Commercial HVAC unit to Bosch, Johnson Controls operates as a pure-play commercial building solutions provider with ~$23B in continuing revenue and solid operating margins (10-14%). However, 10-year GAAP ROIC has averaged 7-10% (median 9.2%) weighed down by $17B+ of goodwill and intangibles dating from the 2016 Tyco merger. Reported cash conversion has been repeatedly depressed by restructuring and separation costs. Balance sheet remains overleveraged with total debt of $9.9B ($8.6B long-term debt) against FY25 net income of $1.7B (LT debt / NI ~5.1x, exceeding the <=4.0x maximum). Management directed the $5.0B net proceeds from the Bosch sale into an accelerated share repurchase rather than deleveraging, failing Gate 6.

current_qualitative.3m: Direct-to-dealer (D2D) distribution model bypasses independent two-step wholesalers for ~75% of sales, embedding high switching costs via Lennox Premier Dealer certification, proprietary diagnostic tools, warranty handling, and co-op marketing. 10-year median ROIC is ~28% with operating margins near 17-18%. Primary erosion threat is private equity contractor consolidation demanding multi-brand wholesale sourcing.
current_qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). While Lennox achieves high returns on capital via its proprietary direct-to-dealer network, structural runway is limited. Capital Goods base-rate persistence is Tier 3 (10-15Y). The rapid private equity consolidation of independent residential HVAC contractors directly threatens Lennox's captive dealer moat by shifting procurement to multi-brand wholesale distributors (Watsco, Ferguson). Exiting Europe leaves Lennox >90% dependent on mature North American residential replacement cycles, with high-ticket consumer financing vulnerable to structural interest rates.
current_qualitative.evidence: 10-year median ROIC of 28.5% with operating margins of 17-18% and FCF of $640M-$785M. Revenue splits ~65% Home Comfort Solutions (Residential) and ~35% Building Climate Solutions (Commercial); ~75% replacement / 25% new construction. However, Lennox is pure-play North American without global scale, competing against Daikin, Carrier, and Trane. Private equity rollups of local HVAC dealers aggregate buying power away from proprietary direct-to-dealer networks.

current_qualitative.3m: Massive proprietary installed base in commercial HVAC, mission-critical Tracer building automation controls, and company-owned direct technician service network create high customer switching costs. Empirically proven by 5-year median ROIC of ~18.5% (ROIC >20% in 2024-2025), robust gross margins, and consistent positive pricing realization (+3-5% annually) driving operating margins from 14% to >18%. Primary erosion threats include low-end residential HVAC commoditization and competition from Asian OEMs in ductless split systems.
current_qualitative.note: Passes all 6 gates. Global leader in commercial HVAC and climate solutions with powerful switching costs anchored by installed base and direct service network. Active beneficiary of AI data center thermal cooling demand and secular building decarbonization/energy efficiency. Clean balance sheet with net debt/NI ~1.2x and interest coverage ~17.5x. [5-10Y g: commercial & data center volume 3.5% + equipment pricing 2.0% + services & controls mix 2.0% - regulatory refrigerant/tariff drag 0.5% + share repurchases 1.5%]
current_qualitative.evidence: 10-year median ROIC ~18.5% with 2024-2025 ROIC >20%. FY2024 revenue $19.8B (+12%), FCF $2.8B (109% conversion); FY2025 revenue $21.3B (+7.5%), operating income $3.97B, net income $2.94B, FCF conversion 98%. Total debt of $4.6B (net debt ~$3.5B) against $2.94B net income yields net debt/NI of 1.19x and interest coverage of 17.5x. Pure-play climate leader benefiting from mission-critical commercial HVAC, data center cooling, and transport refrigeration (Thermo King).

current_qualitative.3m: Spec-in key systems installed base and decentralized acquisition machine. Unrivaled global scale in mechanical and digital access solutions (HID, Yale, effeff). Proven pricing power covering raw metal and wage inflation across multiple cycles. 5-year median GAAP ROIC is 12.5% and operating tangible ROIC exceeds 100% due to serial acquisition intangibles.
current_qualitative.note: Passes all 6 gates. Global leader in physical and electromechanical access solutions with an unassailable installed base in master key systems, architectural spec-in, and HID electronic credentials. Over two-thirds of revenue driven by resilient aftermarket maintenance and replacement. Proven pricing power across multiple inflationary cycles with multi-year FCF conversion >100%. [5-10Y g: aftermarket volume 2.0% + smart access mix 2.0% + pricing power 2.0% + bolt-on M&A 2.0% - restructuring drag 0.5% + buybacks 0.5%]
current_qualitative.evidence: 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 12.5% with tangible operating ROIC >100% due to capital-light assembly and large acquisition intangibles. Owner FCF conversion averaged 119.6% from 2022 to 2025 (FY2025 FCF of 18.6B SEK on 14.7B SEK net income). Net debt / NI sits at 3.07x with 6.98x interest coverage (EBIT 23.1B SEK vs 3.3B SEK interest), easily meeting the <4.0x leverage and >5.0x coverage thresholds.

current_qualitative.3m: Decades of actuator precision engineering and distributor/OEM spec-in. Actuators are a minuscule cost component of building systems but carry catastrophic failure costs, cementing extreme customer loyalty and price insensitivity. Demonstrated multi-year median GAAP ROIC >32% and tangible ROIC >34%.
current_qualitative.note: Passes all 6 gates. Global undisputed hegemon in HVAC damper actuators and control valves. Unbeatable consumer surplus and installer trust: devices represent <2% of building HVAC capex but prevent millions in system downtime, resulting in supreme pricing power. Massive secular tailwinds from data-center liquid cooling and building decarbonization mandates. Pristine debt-free net cash balance sheet with >32% median ROIC. [5-10Y g: volume 5.0% + price 2.0% + data center cooling mix 2.0% - R&D/capex drag 0.5% + buybacks/dividends 0.0%]
current_qualitative.evidence: Multi-cycle GAAP ROIC consistently exceeds 27-36% (median 32.4%), with operating tangible ROIC of 34.2%. Owner EPS grew at a 13.9% CAGR from 2022 to 2025 (reaching 14.77 CHF peak in 2025). Long-term debt is 0.0 CHF against 100.6m CHF in cash, with EBIT / Interest coverage >270x.

current_qualitative.3m: Installer loyalty and decades-evolved training ecosystem. Over 50% European market share in concealed cisterns. Behind-the-wall water damage risk creates insurmountable installer switching costs and pricing power. Multi-year median GAAP ROIC is 30.7% with tangible ROIC of 89.5% and sustained EBITDA margins above 30%.
current_qualitative.note: Passes all 6 gates. Unrivaled European sanitary market hegemon (~50% share in concealed cisterns). Moat anchored by deep plumber installer loyalty, 29 specialized training academies, 50-year spare parts guarantees, and severe behind-the-wall leak liabilities that deter substitution. Maintained 30%+ EBITDA margins and >100% FCF conversion throughout the severe 2022-2025 European construction downturn. Fortress balance sheet with net debt <0.9x NI and interest coverage of 27x. [5-10Y g: European renovation volume 1.5% + pre-wall system penetration 1.5% + pricing power 2.0% - raw material/energy drag 0.5% + share repurchases 0.5%]
current_qualitative.evidence: 5-year median GAAP ROIC is 30.7% with operating tangible ROIC of 89.5%. Multi-year Owner FCF conversion averaged 107.0% (FY2025 FCF of 703.5m CHF on 597.8m CHF net income). Net debt is 505.2m CHF (0.84x NI) with 27.3x interest coverage (EBIT 762.5m CHF vs interest 27.9m CHF).

current_qualitative.3m: Panel manufacturing scale and regulatory product certifications. Dense regional manufacturing network minimizes bulky freight costs. Demonstrated pricing power by passing through massive raw chemical (MDI/polyol/steel) cost inflation in 2021-2023. Multi-year median GAAP ROIC is 14.1% and operating tangible ROIC is 36.7%.
current_qualitative.note: Passes all 6 gates. Global leader in high-performance insulated sandwich panels and advanced building envelopes. Structural moat derived from dense regional manufacturing footprint minimizing bulky transport costs, proprietary QuadCore formulations, and regulatory fire/thermal certifications. Resilient peak-to-peak EPS compounding across European construction cycles backed by EU building decarbonization regulations. Sound balance sheet with net debt of 2.2x NI and 12x interest coverage. [5-10Y g: building efficiency volume 3.5% + QuadCore/data center mix 2.5% + pricing power 2.0% - cyclical/capex drag 0.5% + buybacks 0.5%]
current_qualitative.evidence: 5-year median GAAP ROIC is 14.1% with operating tangible ROIC of 36.7%. Owner EPS compounded consistently from 3.27 EUR in 2022 to a peak of 3.67 EUR in 2025. Multi-year Owner FCF conversion reached 95.7%. Net debt / NI is 2.23x (1,495.8m EUR net debt vs 671.2m EUR NI) with interest coverage of 11.97x (EBIT 929.1m EUR vs interest 77.6m EUR).

current_qualitative.3m: Fails Gate 3b. Heat pump technology has commoditized rapidly, facing severe price competition from Asian HVAC giants (Daikin, Panasonic, Midea) and diversified European heating conglomerates (Bosch, Vaillant). Historical margins and returns were inflated by a temporary, unsustainable European energy subsidy spike (2021-2023). Multi-cycle GAAP ROIC has collapsed to 6-8%, falling far short of the 12% Munger hurdle. Lack of structural pricing power demonstrated by severe margin compression (EBIT margin halved from 15% to 8% in 2024) and inventory write-downs when subsidies waned.
current_qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12%, lack of pricing power). European heat pump demand proved heavily subsidy-dependent, collapsing as gas prices normalized and governments rolled back incentives. NIBE lacks structural pricing power against global Asian scale leaders (Daikin, Panasonic) and diversified European majors (Bosch, Vaillant). Multi-cycle GAAP ROIC compressed to 6-8%, failing the 12% Munger moat proof standard. Waterfall terminates at Gate 3.
current_qualitative.evidence: Operating margin collapsed from 14.9% in 2023 to 8.0% in 2024, with organic sales dropping -13%. Return on capital employed (ROCE) dropped to 6.8%-8.5% in 2024 and consensus multi-year ROIC tracking at 5.7%-6.2% when accounting for acquisition goodwill. Unable to maintain price or volume in the absence of government subsidies.

current_qualitative.3m: Fails Gate 3b. While stone wool provides superior fire resistance, insulation is fundamentally an energy-intensive industrial commodity facing direct substitution from fiberglass (Owens Corning, Saint-Gobain) and polyurethane/phenolic foams (Kingspan). Customers have virtually zero switching costs between certified insulation materials. Margins and unit economics are highly volatile and heavily exposed to natural gas, coke, and electricity input costs. Furthermore, capital intensity of melting rock at 1,500°C creates high ongoing reinvestment burdens without pricing power above inflation across full economic cycles.
current_qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Moat proof & commodity substitution). Stone wool insulation is an energy-intensive industrial commodity lacking customer switching costs or toll-booth barriers. End-customers readily substitute alternative insulation materials (fiberglass, foam, wood fiber). Vulnerability to volatile fossil energy input costs (gas, electricity, coke) and heavy ongoing capital intensity required for furnace decarbonization prevent durable pricing power above inflation across the full cycle. Waterfall terminates at Gate 3.
current_qualitative.evidence: Manufacturing stone wool requires continuous melting of basalt rock at >1,500°C, exposing gross margins to extreme European energy cost volatility. High capital expenditure requirements for furnace maintenance, emissions abatement, and localized plants dilutes owner earnings. Zero customer switching costs once building specifications are met.

current_qualitative.3m: Local manufacturing and distribution footprint creates a regional barrier due to weight-to-value transport economics in gypsum and insulation. However, cyclical exposure to new residential construction and capital intensity prevent sustained excess returns, with 5-year median GAAP ROIC hovering around 6-8%, well below the 12% hurdle.
current_qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12%, REJECT). Heavy building products and materials manufacturer benefits from local plant density and energy-efficiency renovation demand, but structural capital intensity and cyclical new-build construction limit multi-cycle GAAP ROIC to ~6-8%.
current_qualitative.evidence: Multi-cycle GAAP ROIC hovers around 6.0-7.5% (GuruFocus), well below the 12% threshold despite portfolio pruning (divesting UK distribution, expanding in construction chemicals via Chryso and GCP). Group operating margin reached 11.4% in 2024, but goodwill and capital intensity dilute overall returns on capital.

current_qualitative.3m: North American LTL network density across ~370 service centers and linehaul lanes creates scale economies shared. Proof of moat shown by 3-year median GAAP ROIC of 45.8% (FY23: 69.9%, FY24: 45.8%, FY25: 12.9%) and annual 4.9-5.9% General Rate Increases (GRIs). Primary erosion threats include low-cost non-union competitors (ODFL, Saia), shipper TMS spot-bidding, and cyclical freight downturns.
current_qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 10, REJECT). North American LTL network density (~370 terminals) provides operational scale economies shared and historical median GAAP ROIC of 45.8%. However, the business faces active, unhedged terminal headwinds across three macrotrends: chronic commercial driver shortages and labor cost inflation (Macrotrend 2), capital-intensive diesel fleet decarbonization and zero-emission mandates (Macrotrend 4), and high capital intensity compounded by $4.26B in carveout debt (Macrotrend 5). Capped at CAP = 10 by the Rule of Secular Resilience, failing the 15-year hurdle.
current_qualitative.evidence: FedEx Freight (NYSE: FDXF) was spun off from FedEx Corp in June 2026 as an independent publicly traded company. Operates North America's largest LTL network with $8.8B-$9.4B in annual revenue across ~370 service centers. 3-year median GAAP ROIC of 45.8% (FY23: 69.9%, FY24: 45.8%, FY25: 12.9%) and tangible ROIC median >60% demonstrate historical network moat, maintained through disciplined 4.9-5.9% annual General Rate Increases (GRIs). However, FY25 EBIT declined 62% to $540M and OCF fell to $167M (Owner FCF -$225M) amidst freight cyclicality. The business faces structural terminal labor constraints (truck driver scarcity), mandatory diesel fleet transition capex under EPA/CARB rules, and a heavy post-spin debt burden ($4.26B LT debt vs $655M TTM net income, with -$497M negative equity resulting from a pre-spin debt dividend to parent FedEx). Under the 5-Macrotrend framework, persistent labor and energy transition headwinds cap CAP at 10 years, failing Gate 4.

current_qualitative.3m: Scale economies shared in North American domestic intermodal (>100k containers) and private fleet replacement (DCS). However, JBHT lacks independent pricing power; intermodal must maintain a discount to highway trucking, making JBHT a price-taker during freight downturns when overcapacity triggers aggressive spot discounting.
current_qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Pricing Power & Proof of Moat, REJECT). North American intermodal and dedicated transportation leader with scale economies shared, but lacks invariant pricing power across the cycle. Intermodal rates must price at a discount to over-the-road trucking; during freight recessions and capacity gluts, JBHT becomes a cyclical price-taker, causing severe margin compression (operating margin fell from 9.4% in 2022 to 6.9% in 2024) and dragging trough ROIC below the 12% hurdle (11.2% in 2024).
current_qualitative.evidence: 10-year median ROIC is ~13.8%, but cyclical: 21.6% in 2022 (freight peak), 14.6% in 2023, 11.2% in 2024 (below 12% hurdle), and 12.4% in 2025. Operating margins compressed from 9.4% in 2022 to 6.9% in 2024. Intermodal (JBI, ~47% of revenue) and Dedicated (DCS, ~32% of revenue) provide operating scale and multi-year contract stability, but brokerage (ICS) and truckload (JBT) are exposed to brutal spot rate competition. CapEx cycles for container and tractor fleet replacement create lumpy FCF (-$118M in 2023, +$618M in 2024, +$948M in 2025). Net debt of ~$1.0B is manageable (EBIT interest coverage >10x), but structural inability to price above inflation in freight downcycles fails Gate 3b.

current_qualitative.3m: Self-reinforcing network density and irreplaceable physical terminal footprint (250+ owned/zoned cross-dock service centers) create massive scale economies shared. Unmatched service execution (99% on-time delivery, 0.1% cargo claims ratio vs industry average 1.5%) drives durable pricing power (revenue per cwt up 4-6% p.a. across all freight cycles). 5-year median GAAP ROIC is 32.7% (24.4% in 2025 trough) with best-in-class operating ratio (70-75% vs 85-95% for peers). Erosion threats from freight recessions or price wars are blunted by ODFL's premium service brand and low-cost non-union structure.
current_qualitative.note: Passes all 6 gates. The undisputed premier less-than-truckload (LTL) motor carrier in North America with an unreplicable nationwide terminal network, 99% on-time delivery, industry-leading operating ratio, net-cash balance sheet, and proven pricing power above inflation across freight cycles. Beneficiary of supply chain reshoring and insulated from AI disruption. current_qualitative.evidence: 10-year track record of industry-leading capital efficiency: 10-year GAAP and Tangible ROIC averaged >27% (peak 40.1% in 2022, trough 24.4% in 2025).
